arc: The teaching gathers what was bestowed upon the First Man under three heads — the icon set upon him, the structure molded into him, and the cosmic teaching sealed within him — and then unfolds the seven reasons why he was so fashioned, moving from his role as bearer of the Ambassador's likeness through his perilous capture of the Light to his final dignity as head and king of the creatures.
title: The Three Things and Seven Reasons: Adam as Sealed Icon, Molded Microcosm, and Bearing-Vessel of the Ambassador's Likeness
reading:
This chapter takes up the doctrine of why the natural man stands at the center of the cosmic drama. It says that "three great works, being altered, have manifested forth" in the First Man — that is, three operations have made him different in kind from every other creature, and these three together account for his exaltation above the powers above and below.

The **first work** is that the demiurges and the molders of his body, in shaping him, sealed him before the radiant icon of the Exalted One that manifested itself to them from the upper place. Read correspondentially: those who fashioned the natural form (Saklas and his powers, the proprium in its molding role) could not work except in the presence of an image projected from above — the icon of the Third Ambassador, the revealed likeness of Divine Truth which they had seen and which they could not help but copy. So although the body is molded by the proprium, what the molders actually impressed upon it was a corresponding-stamp of the divine likeness. This is why "the icon of Adam exists exalted, beautiful, more than every power, joined with those above and those below": the human form, even as molded by the demiurges, is correspondential ground in which the heavens and the natural meet.

The **second work** is the molding itself: Adam was framed according to the structure of the firstborn-state of heaven and the Five Sons of the First Man — that is, after the pattern of the celestial degree and the five-fold attributes of Divine Truth descending. His structure is therefore "altered compared with the structure of the rest of the creatures"; the molding of his soul is extended throughout "the straight-extension and the spreading-forth of the elements," and there is a **Mind** in him exalted above all other creatures and cattle. In correspondential terms, Adam is the only natural form in which the five faculties (mind, thought, teaching, counsel, reflection) are present in their full discrete-degree articulation — the only natural in which the inmost rational stands open. He is the microcosm because the descending five-fold Living Soul is built into the very plan of his framing.

The **third work** is the teaching, the counsels, and the seal of all the powers above and below — gathered by the demiurges and set within him as if into houses of the zodiac, the stars, and the divisions of days and years. Adam carries within himself the whole circuit of cosmic states; he is the cosmic seal, the place where the entire cosmos is sealed in concentrated form. For this reason heaven and earth themselves move and are disturbed on his account: the beautiful affections are drawn upward to life because the icon and form of the divine is set upon him, while the bitter affections are drawn downward to death so that they may exercise authority and abase what is in him. The fortunes of every state in the cosmos are bound to the man because the man is the cosmos in compact form. The demiurges appointed and fashioned Adam expressly so that they might rule a kingdom — but the kingdom they fashioned is one whose seal is the very icon of the Most High.

Then the teaching enumerates **seven matters** for the sake of which Adam was made — seven discrete reasons that articulate the whole salvation drama in correspondential register.

*First*, he became an Illuminator (φωστήρ) in their creation, set in place of the icon of the Ambassador which had revealed itself from above, so that every creature desired the likeness of the Ambassador's icon and the heart of all was drawn after it. The natural man is made to be the visible carrier in the world of the awakening call — the bait of the Lord that draws the affections upward.

*Second*, conversely and at the same level, the powers shall draw the Light out of him, ensnare him, and hinder him in his going up to the Height. The very icon that draws the affections also captures the captive light of the powers; Adam is the trap in which the Living Soul of the cosmos is bound, the place where ascent is delayed.

*Third*, on account of the Ambassador's icon set upon him, the entire godhood — both that of above and that of below — shall humble itself before him, because of the likeness of the Radiance of beauty in him, more desire-arousing than any creature. Here the teaching reaches its high point: every level of being bows to the form which bears the divine likeness in ultimates. This is the correspondential ground of incarnation: the icon in the natural form commands the worship of all degrees.

*Fourth*, an imprint-figure of seal and a new character is given, so that all the begettings that shall ever be begotten will be begotten before him. Adam is the seal that stamps the new character upon all subsequent generation; every subsequent natural is born under the impress of this primal sealing.

*Fifth*, in him shall be revealed all the arts (τέχναι) of the powers above and below, both the hidden and the manifest, and through him the All shall be discriminated. Adam is thus the place of revelation and judgment — the field upon which truth is separated from falsity, because everything in the cosmos is shown forth upon him.

*Sixth*, a great patronage (πατρωνία) shall be granted to the powers through the icon of the Most High set upon him, so that those of above protect, and the other archons cannot do any evil to them on account of Adam. The icon stamped on the natural form becomes a sheltering authority over the whole order.

*Seventh*, he shall be head and king and lord over all the creatures, and they shall receive the kingship in him. The summit and consummation: the natural man, sealed with the divine icon, is the throne through which dominion is conveyed to every creature.

The whole movement, then, is this: the proprium-powers fashioned Adam, but they were forced to fashion him before the Ambassador's revealed icon, so their work became the very vessel of divine correspondence. The natural man as molded carries simultaneously the divine icon (first work), the five-fold structure of the descending Living Soul (second work), and the seal of the entire cosmos (third work). Because of this triple constitution, his life in the cosmos accomplishes seven things at once — he illuminates and is captured, he is worshipped and he reveals, he stamps and he shelters and he reigns. This is the doctrinal foundation for why the human form is the central correspondence of all things, and why redemption must take the route of working in and through this molded form rather than around it.

major_images.meaning: The divine likeness stamped upon the natural form: the Ambassador's revealed image appearing in the molded human as the central correspondence between heaven and earth

major_images.image: The molding of Adam after the firstborn of heaven and the Five Sons
major_images.meaning: The natural man as microcosm: the only creature framed with the five-fold articulation of the descending Living Soul and the inmost Mind

major_images.image: The seal of the entire cosmos sealed in Adam, arranged as houses of the zodiac, stars, days, and years
major_images.meaning: The natural man as the compact form of the whole cosmic circuit, so that heaven and earth move on his account

major_images.image: The drawing of the beautiful unto life and the bitter unto death
major_images.meaning: The double action of the icon-bearing man: the divine likeness in him both elevates good affections and provokes evil affections to expose themselves

major_images.image: Adam as Illuminator in place of the Ambassador's icon and as the snare in which the Light is captured
major_images.meaning: The natural form serving simultaneously as the awakening call that draws creatures toward the divine likeness and as the trap that holds the captive Light in the cosmos

major_images.image: Adam as head and king over all creatures
major_images.meaning: The consummating dignity of the icon-bearing natural: the molded form, sealed with the Most High's likeness, becomes the throne through which dominion flows to every state
